display.title: Episode 533: Greasing the Wheels During Davening (Parshas Behaaloscha)
display.summary_short: A lesson from Parshas Behaaloscha: keep rising higher like the menorah's flames. Then Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev finds only good in a coachman greasing his wagon in tallis and tefillin.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Parshas Behaaloscha. Uncle Yossi explains the Alter Rebbe's teaching that we must "live with the times", with the weekly parsha, and draws a lesson from the kindling of the menorah. The Torah says "when you raise up the lights": every neshamah is a candle that brings light into the world through Torah and mitzvos, and like the menorah's flames it must keep reaching higher, so a soldier of Tzivos Hashem never rests on the rank already earned. Since the Kohen lit all seven lamps, we must also help friends and relatives shine, bringing Moshiach closer. After the Hakochainik march, a seven-year-old guest from Michigan leads the Shema, everyone gives tzedakah, and a sponsor message follows. Story time: a crowd outside shul is shocked to see a coachman greasing his wagon wheels while wearing tallis and tefillin. Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev instead praises the man for loving Hashem so much that he wears tallis and tefillin even while he works, teaching us to judge everyone favorably. The show closes with Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery, advice on choosing a Torah-observant summer camp, an invitation to send compositions, and Shabbos candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Always judge others favorably and look for their good qualities; and in Torah and mitzvos, keep growing higher every day.
